1. (Currently Amended) An assembly comprising a test tube with an affixed MTP __that is not disclosed in Maxell Corp. of America__.

2. (Original) The assembly of claim 1, wherein the MTP is embedded in the test tube.

3. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 1, wherein the MTP is embedded underneath __the bottom of__ the test tube, oriented for reading downwards.

4. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 1, wherein the test tube is a biorepository test tube __designed for long-term storage of biological samples at cryogenic temperatures__.

5. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 1, wherein the MTP is embedded in polypropylene or acetal polymer __and wherein the polypropylene or acetal polymer is selected to maintain structural integrity and readability of the MTP at temperatures of -20°C or below__.

6. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 1, wherein the MTP is embedded near the center bottom of the __test tube__.

(Currently Amended) A system for storing samples and comprising of the assembly of claim 1, and __at least two of__ the following: a rack for biorepository test tubes; __an__ automated robot for moving racks or biorepository test tubes; and __an__ automated sampling device adapted to sample said racks or biorepository test tubes __wherein the automated robot and automated sampling device are integrated to enable automated tracking and retrieval of samples using the embedded MTP__.

14. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 13 adapted for low temperature operation, such that the racks/test tubes are handled at -20°C or less __and wherein the embedded MTP remains readable at such temperatures__.

19. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 4, wherein the MTP is embedded in polypropylene or acetal polymer __and wherein the polypropylene or acetal polymer is selected to maintain structural integrity and readability of the MTP at temperatures of -20°C or below__.

20. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 19, wherein the MTP is embedded near the center bottom of the __test tube__.
